questions.stem:
The discrete random variable $X$ has probability function $\mathrm{p}(x)$ and cumulative distribution function $\mathrm{F}(x)$ given in the table below.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline x & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5\\ \hline \mathrm{p}(x) & 0.10 & a & 0.28 & c & 0.24\\ \hline \mathrm{F}(x) & 0.10 & 0.26 & b & 0.76 & d\\ \hline\end{array}$

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) B1: $(d=)1$
Official notes (completeness pass):
- B1 for sight of 1 referring to $d$ (may be in table or in the question)

parts.label: b
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) M1: $a=0.26-0.1$ or $b=0.26+0.28$ or 'a'$+0.38$ or $0.76-$'c' or $c=0.76-$'b' or $1-(0.62+$'a'$)$
A1: any two of $a=0.16$, $b=0.54$, $c=0.22$ correct
A1: all three values correct
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 for any correct calculation seen (may be implied by one correct answer) ft their values for 'a', 'b' or 'c' Do not award if answer is $<0$ or $>1$

parts.label: d
parts.text:
Two independent observations, $X_1$ and $X_2$, are taken from the distribution of $X$.
(d) Find the probability that $X_1$ and $X_2$ are both odd.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) $\mathrm{P}(X\text{ is an odd number})=0.1+0.28+0.24=0.62$
M1: $\mathrm{P}(X_1\text{ and }X_2\text{ both odd})=0.62^2$
A1: $=0.3844$ awrt 0.384
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 for $(0.1+0.28+0.24)^2$ oe i.e. must be a complete correct expression e.g. $(1-['a'+'c'])^2$ and ft their values for 'a' and 'c'
- A1 for awrt 0.384 or exact fraction $\frac{961}{2500}$

parts.label: e
parts.text:
Given that $X_1$ and $X_2$ are both odd,
(e) find the probability that the sum of $X_1$ and $X_2$ is 6
Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(e) M1: for attempt at correct conditional probability i.e. a correct ratio of probabilities stated in words that mentions both $X_1$ and $X_2$; may be implied by a numerical ratio with correct numerator and their "(d)" on denominator (this would score M1A1ft)
$\mathrm{P}(X_1+X_2=6\mid\text{both odd})=\dfrac{\mathrm{P}(X_1+X_2=6\cap X_1,X_2\text{ odd})}{\mathrm{P}(X_1,X_2\text{ odd})}=\dfrac{0.1\times0.24+0.28\times0.28+0.24\times0.1}{\text{'(d)'}}=\dfrac{0.1264}{\text{'(d)'}}$
A1ft: correct numerator $0.1264$ over $0.384..$, or correct numerator and denominator of their 'd'
A1: $=0.328824141..$ awrt 0.329, or exact fraction $\frac{316}{961}$

questions.stem:
A sports teacher recorded the number of press-ups done by his students in two minutes. He recorded this information for a Year 7 class and for a Year 11 class.
The back-to-back stem and leaf diagram shows this information.
$\begin{array}{ccc}\text{Totals} & \text{Year 7 class} & \quad\quad\text{Year 11 class}\\ (6) & 8\ 7\ 6\ 5\ 5\ 4 \mid 1 & \\ (10) & 9\ 7\ 7\ 6\ 5\ 4\ 4\ 4\ 2\ 2 \mid 2 \mid 0\ 5\ 6\ 9 & (4)\\ (7) & 8\ 7\ 5\ 4\ 3\ 3\ 0 \mid 3 \mid 3\ 4\ 5\ 8\ 8 & (5)\\ (5) & 9\ 9\ 7\ 2\ 2 \mid 4 \mid 0\ 5\ 6\ 7\ 9 & (5)\\ (3) & 8\ 4\ 0 \mid 5 \mid 0\ 3\ 5\ 5\ 6\ 6\ 7\ 7\ 7\ 9\ 9 & (11)\\ & \mid 6 \mid 0\ 3\ 3\ 3\ 3\ 4\ 8 & (7)\end{array}$
Key: $2|4|0$ means 42 press-ups for a Year 7 student and 40 press-ups for a Year 11 student

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the median number of press-ups for each class.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) B1: Year 7 median $=29$
B1: Year 11 median $=54$
Official notes (completeness pass):
- In (a) at least one of the values should be assigned to a Year group. If you see just "29" and "54" award SC B1B0
- 1st B1 for 29 seen (may be circled on diag.) 2nd B1 for 54 seen

parts.label: b
parts.text:
For the Year 11 class, the lower quartile is 38 and the upper quartile is 59
(b) Find the lower quartile and the upper quartile for the Year 7 class.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) B1: [Lower quartile =] 22
B1: [Upper quartile =] 42
Official notes (completeness pass):
- 1st B1 for 22 and 2nd B1 for 42 (these values may be circled on the diagram)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Use the medians and quartiles to describe the skewness of each of the two distributions.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) M1: for a comparison for either year using quartiles only, either "$Q_3-Q_2>Q_2-Q_1$ and positive skew" or "$Q_3-Q_2<Q_2-Q_1$ and negative skew"
Year 7: $Q_3-Q_2 (=13)>Q_2-Q_1 (=7)$: A1 Positive skew
Year 11: $Q_3-Q_2 (=5)<Q_2-Q_1 (=16)$: A1 Negative skew
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Statements should be compatible with their values
- 1st A1 for Year 7 clearly labelled "positive skew"(both words) ("correlation" is A0) 2nd A1 for Year 11 clearly labelled "negative skew"(both words) ("correlation" is A0)
- Ans. only: If no comparison is stated then award M1A1A1 only if both statements are correct and compatible with their medians and quartiles so score is 0 or 3

parts.label: d
parts.text:
(d) Give two reasons why the normal distribution should not be used to model the number of press-ups done by the Year 11 class.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) B1: Data is skewed
B1: Data is not continuous
Official notes (completeness pass):
- 1st B1 for a statement mentioning (or implying) that the data is skew (or not symmetric) Ignore ref to +ve or - ve
- SC Allow for statement "mean $\neq$ median" if mean = 48.8 and median = 54 or 53 seen
- 2nd B1 for a statement mentioning data is not continuous (allow identifiable spelling) Allow "this data is discrete" for 2nd B1
- NB means Year 7 $\bar{x}=31.5$ Year 11 $\bar{x}=48.8$

questions.stem:
Events $A$ and $B$ are shown in the Venn diagram below
where $x$, $y$, 0.10 and 0.32 are probabilities.
[Venn diagram: circle $A$ containing $x$ and, in the overlap with $B$, $0.10$; circle $B$ containing $y$; outside both circles, $0.32$.]

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find an expression in terms of $x$ for
(i) $\mathrm{P}(A)$
(ii) $\mathrm{P}(B\mid A)$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a)(i) B1: $x+0.1$ [P$(x+0.1)$ is B0]
(a)(ii) M1: for a correct ratio of probabilities formula with at least one correct probability value (may ft their (a)(i) in the denominator) or a prob ratio of the form $\dfrac{0.1}{\text{(a)(i)}}$
$\mathrm{P}(B\mid A)=\dfrac{\mathrm{P}(B\cap A)}{\mathrm{P}(A)}=\dfrac{0.1}{x+0.1}$
A1: $\dfrac{0.1}{x+0.1}$ as their final answer
Official notes (completeness pass):
- If num' > denom' score M0. NB P$(A)=0.68-y$ and P$(B|A)=\dfrac{0.1}{0.68-y}$ is B0M1A0

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find an expression in terms of $x$ and $y$ for $\mathrm{P}(A\cup B)$
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) B1: $x+y+0.1$ (o.e.) [P$(x+y+0.1)$ is B0]
Official notes (completeness pass):
- B1 for any correct expression in $x$ and $y$ e.g. $0.1+x+0.1+y-0.1$ Condone $x+y+0.1=1-0.32$ or 0.68 since LHS is a correct expression

parts.label: c
parts.text:
Given that $\mathrm{P}(A)=2\mathrm{P}(B)$
(c) find the value of $x$ and the value of $y$
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) M1: using sum of probs. $=1$ to form a "correct" linear equation in $x$ and $y$ [$x+y=0.58$]; ft their (b) and/or their (a)(i) e.g. "(a)(i)" $+0.32+y=1$
M1: using $\mathrm{P}(A)=2\mathrm{P}(B)$ to form a "correct" linear equation in $x$ and $y$ [$x-2y=0.1$]; ft their P$(A)$ from part (a)
M1: for an attempt to solve their 2 linear equations, implied by 2 correct Ms and correct answer; requires correct algebraic steps leading to an equation in one variable
A1: $x=0.42$ (following correct working and dependent on 1st 2 Ms)
A1: $y=0.16$ (following correct working and dependent on 1st 2 Ms)
SC: $\mathrm{P}(A)=0.68-y=2(y+0.1)$ scores M2 (2nd and 3rd Ms) and 2nd A1 when $y=0.16$ seen; sight of $x+y+0.1=0.68$ (o.e.) scores 1st M1 and then 1st A1 if $x=0.42$ follows
Official notes (completeness pass):
- $x+y+0.1+0.32=1$ or $x+y+0.1=0.68$ or "(b)" $+0.32=1$ o.e. M1; $x+0.1=2(y+0.1)$ M1; Eliminating $x$ gives $3y=0.48$ M1
- If they use 2P$(A)$ = P$(B)$ or swap $x$ and $y$ score 2nd M0 but allow access to 3rd M
- If there are not 2 equations this cannot be scored (but see SC)
- Beware $0.42=0.32+0.1$ so answer only does not score full marks
- or P$(A)=x+0.1=2(0.68-x)$ score M2 (2nd and 3rd Ms) and 1st A1 when $x=0.42$ seen. Sight of $x+y+0.1=0.68$ (o.e.)(scores 1st M1) and then 2nd A1 if $y=0.16$ follows.
